test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-2) Official Paper (Held On: 13 June 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A goods train overtakes two boys who are walking in the same direction in which the train is going, at a rate of 5 kmph and 10 kmph and passes them completely in 21 and 24 seconds respectively. What is the length of the goods train (in metres)?
solution:
**Given:**

Speed of the first person = 5 km/h

Speed of the second person = 10 km/h

Train taken to overtake the first person = 21 sec

Train taken to overtake the second person = 24 sec

**Concept used:**

Speed = Distance/Time

km/h × 5/18 = m/sec

When two bodies move in the same direction, then Relative speed = the Difference in their speeds

**Calculation:**

Let the length and the speed of a train be L m/sec and V m respectively.

Speed of the first person in m/sec = 5 × 5/18 = 25/18 m/sec

Speed of the second person in m/sec = 10 × 5/18 = 25/9 m/sec

Now,

Relative speed of the train and the first person = {V – (25/18)} m/sec

So,

V – (25/18) = L/21

⇒ V = L/21 + 25/18 ----(1)

Again,

Relative speed of the train and the second person = {V – (25/9)}m/sec

So,

{V – (25/9)} = L/24 

⇒ V = L/24 + 25/9 ----(2)

From eq (1) and eq (2) we can say,

L/21 + 25/18 = L/24 + 25/9

⇒ L/21 – L/24 = 25/9 – 25/18

⇒ (8L – 7L)/(168) = (50 – 25)/(18)

⇒ (L)/168 = 25/18 

⇒ L = (25/18) × 168

⇒ L = 233(1)/(3) m

**∴ The length of the train is 233(1)/(3) m.**
